title: The natural-valued limit approximant must return the observed output, not merely a halting bit.
details: Miller2008 Lemma28.1, displayed forward-direction f(n,s) on p57, visually checked2026-11-10. The theorem concerns arbitrary natural-valued g computable from halting, but the displayed f is1 whenever the bounded oracle computation converges and0 otherwise. For the constant-two g this f is always0 or1 and cannot converge to2. Replace the successful branch by the actual bounded computation output, retaining0 as the failure default. Finite-use replay then gives eventual equality to g(n), and the construction relativizes with the same output convention.
